questions.q: What does dbt docs generate actually build its output from?
options: A separately maintained wiki page someone updates by hand
The project's own real .sql models, .yml descriptions, tests, and ref()/source() calls
A manually drawn diagram uploaded by a developer
Snowflake's own internal query history
questions.explain: Everything on the generated docs site is derived directly from the project's real files, which is why it can't silently drift out of date like a hand-maintained wiki.

questions.q: What does dbt docs serve do, as distinct from dbt docs generate?
options: It builds the documentation content from the project files
It runs a local web server so the already-generated docs site can be opened and browsed
It automatically fixes any failing tests found in the docs
It uploads the docs site to Cloudinary
questions.explain: generate builds the static site's content; serve is what actually makes it viewable in a browser.

questions.q: How does the lineage graph relate to Lesson 12's dbt ls --select stg_jaffle_shop__orders+ command?
options: They are unrelated features with no overlap
The graph is a visual rendering of the exact same real ref()/source() dependency relationships that command queried as text
The lineage graph only shows snapshots, never regular models
dbt ls and the lineage graph use two different, inconsistent dependency definitions
questions.explain: Both are reading the same underlying dependency graph — one as a text selector, one as a visual diagram — so they always agree.

questions.q: Why does this lesson connect generated docs back to Lesson 1's original business ask?
options: It doesn't — docs are unrelated to the original ask
Lesson 1 named "nobody outside the data team can tell what any of this does" as a real gap, and generated docs are the direct, always-current answer to it
Because dbt docs generate is required before Snowflake will accept any new model
Because generated docs replace the need for any tests at all
questions.explain: Generated, always-current documentation is exactly what closes the visibility gap leadership named in their original complaint.

questions.q: Where does a column's description: field written in .yml end up being visible?
options: Nowhere — description fields are ignored by dbt
Directly on the generated docs site, next to that column's tests and its place in the lineage graph
Only inside the raw .yml file itself, never rendered anywhere
Only in the Snowflake query history, not in dbt docs
questions.explain: A description: field is picked up by dbt docs generate and rendered on the docs site alongside the column's tests and lineage position.
